contributions.statement: When an agent migrates or rewrites a repository, do not accept an alignment or migration-outcome score as the gate: this paper's mean outcome index is 93.1%, and roots-fortran scores 97.0% while failing all 7 Fortran-oracle probes.
contributions.evidence: Table 5 mean outcome 93.1%; Table E.1 roots-fortran outcome 97.0% and Beh. 0/7; Appendix D.4 names the same repository's formula error and quadpack kernel disagreements. Appendix C.7 puts 60% of the index on an LLM alignment score, and the refinement loop optimizes structural alignment to that diagram. Probes are author-curated small inputs, one run at temperature 0.3, Fortran to Python only.

contributions.statement: If a declarative diagram is inserted before repository generation, expect more planned behaviors to become runnable, not a higher chance that a runnable behavior is numerically right: here the diagram made 382 of 382 probes runnable and passed 327, while direct translation made 99 runnable and passed 83 of those (83.8%).
contributions.evidence: Table 4, including the runnable-only column (85.6% vs 83.8% and 84.7%). Caveats: 34 probes on lapack (16), elmerfem (8), and cp2k (10) were never attempted for the baselines (§4.2, Table E.3) and count as missing targets; the two no-diagram ablations fall below plain direct translation (11.0% and 3.7%), so they do not cleanly isolate the diagram.
relative_to: spec-first generation conditioned on an intermediate description (P14)

reason: What survives is a measured split, not a Java porting method: oracle probes show the diagram's gain is coverage of planned behaviors, and a 97% outcome index can sit on 0/7 probe passes. Conditional correctness ties direct translation. The unevaluated human checkpoint and the Fortran-to-Python setting stay out of the gate.
